sectors.name: FMCG
sectors.blurb: Staples compound through cycles; the sector's sin is paying 40x+ for certainty. The knife falls in a bad monsoon or an input-cost spike.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.blurb: Multi-decade switching-cost annuities priced off US/EM spend. The cycle: campus hiring booms, dollar rupee swings, and client-budget freezes that are noise, not structure.

sectors.name: Power & Capital Goods
sectors.blurb: India's capex cycle with order books as the truth serum. Regulated returns cap the upside; execution slippage and receivables are where the knives hide.

sectors.name: Retail & Discretionary
sectors.blurb: Unorganized-to-organized transition is the whole thesis: Titan in jewelry, DMart in groceries, Zudio in apparel. Priced for that transition twice over — hence the brutal reality check.

companies.name: Reliance Industries (Retail)
companies.note: Conglomerate proxy — the listed way to own Reliance Retail's organized-transition story.

sectors.name: Banking & Financials
sectors.blurb: A bank is a leveraged moat: deposit franchise is everything. Cheap on book rarely means cheap in reality — watch credit costs, not the P/B trap.

sectors.name: Pharma & Healthcare
sectors.blurb: US generics are a commodity knife-fight; India-branded formulations are the moat. FDA warnings and price erosion make the drops — the India franchise makes the recovery.

narratives.TITAN: Titan runs Tanishq, the jewelry brand that converted India's unorganized gold market into a trusted, hallmarking-led chain — a textbook unorganized-to-organized transition. It belongs in a Coffee Can because the brand compounds family savings into annuity-like store economics, but you pay a permanent premium for that quality.
narratives.DMART: DMart runs India's most cost-disciplined grocery chain, sacrificing glamour for everyday-low-price density around stores it owns. The cultural moat is the frugality itself — competitors can copy the layout, not the patience.
narratives.HDFCBANK: HDFC Bank built India's most conservative deposit franchise and refuses to chase yield for growth's sake. The cultural moat is underwriting discipline; you buy it to sleep well, not to double fast.
narratives.TCS: TCS is the default outsourcer for global banks and airlines, with decade-long contracts that make revenue an annuity. The switching cost is real: replacing TCS mid-program is a board-level event, so it rarely happens.
narratives.ITC: ITC monetizes cigarettes — a regulated near-duopoly that funds a growing FMCG and hotels empire essentially for free. The moat is regulatory capture of distribution; the risk is the same regulation, and that is why it is permanently cheap.
narratives.SUNPHARMA: Sun Pharma scaled from generics into specialty (glatiramer, Ilumya) with an India-branded base that funds US R&D. It is the sector's quality compounder — priced accordingly.
narratives.NTPC: NTPC owns the largest conventional power fleet in India and sells into contracted PPAs with state utilities. Returns are regulated and slow — a bond with a dividend, not a compounder, and it belongs in the defensive slot only when the P/E is humble.
narratives.POWERGRID: Power Grid owns most of India's transmission corridors — a regulated near-monopoly on the country's electricity highways. The moat is the ROW (right of way) you cannot replicate; the growth is the capex cycle.
narratives.HAL: HAL is the monopoly supplier of India's military aircraft programs, with order books stretching years into Make-in-India spending. It is a state franchise, not a business — price it like a government bond with equity risk.
narratives.BEL: BEL holds the defense electronics franchise — radars, communication gear — with competitors kept out by procurement rules. Monopoly economics, PSU execution; the knife falls on order-announcement gaps, not fundamentals.
narratives.RELIANCE: Reliance Retail is executing India's largest unorganized-to-organized retail transition, funded by O2C cash flows. The stock is the conglomerate, not the store — accept the blended P/E or wait for a deep correction.
narratives.PVRINOX: PVR INOX is the merged near-monopoly of Indian premium multiplexes. Box-office is the cycle; screen-ownership and ads are the moat — a mediocre compounder at a fair price is better than this at a great one.
narratives.MANKIND: Mankind built India's largest prescription-led mass-market pharma franchise by pricing chronic medicines for tier-2/3 India. Doctor relationships at that density are a brand moat no newcomer can buy.
narratives.KALYANKJIL: Kalyan Jewellers is the #2 branded jewelry play riding the same hallmarking transition as Titan, at a fraction of the valuation. The moat is thinner and debt real — a discount story, not a quality one.
narratives.SIEMENS: Siemens India sits on decades of installed industrial automation base — factories replace, they don't switch. The moat is the installed base; the cycle is capex orders.
narratives.TRENT: Trent scaled Zudio into India's fastest-growing value-fashion chain with landed-cost economics rivals can't match. The transition story is real; the multiple already believes it.
